questions.question: A project network is directed and acyclic from start $S$ to finish $T$; each edge is an activity with a duration, and activities leaving a vertex wait for all activities entering it. There are no resource restrictions. Which quantity equals the shortest possible project duration?
options: The length of a longest $S$-$T$ path
The length of a shortest $S$-$T$ path
The sum of all activity durations
The length of the path with most edges

questions.question: In a project network from $S$ to $T$, each edge is an activity with a duration. At vertex $v$ three activities enter, finishing at times 4, 9 and 6, and one activity leaves $v$. When can the leaving activity start at the earliest?
options: At time 4, when the first entering activity finishes
At time 6, the middle of the three finishing times
At time 9, when the last entering activity finishes
At time 19, after the three times are added up

questions.question: A project network is directed and acyclic from start $S$ to finish $T$; each edge is an activity with a duration, and activities leaving a vertex wait for all activities entering it. A binary variable $x_{ij}$ selects edge $(i,j)$ with duration $d_{ij}$, and flow-balance constraints make the selected edges an $S$-$T$ path. Which objective gives the project duration?
options: Make $\sum d_{ij}x_{ij}$ as small as possible
Use as few selected edges $\sum x_{ij}$ as it can
Make the constant $\sum d_{ij}$ as large as possible
Make $\sum d_{ij}x_{ij}$ as large as possible

questions.question: In the binary model of an acyclic project network from $S$ to $T$, $x_{ij}=1$ if edge $(i,j)$ is selected, and each vertex $v$ gets the constraint (outgoing selected edges) $-$ (incoming selected edges) $=b_v$. Which right-hand sides make the selection an $S$-$T$ path?
options: $b_S=b_T=1$, $b_v=0$ elsewhere: both path ends count once
$b_S=1$, $b_T=-1$, $b_v=0$ elsewhere: one unit from $S$ to $T$
$b_v=1$ everywhere: every vertex sends one unit onward
$b_S=-1$, $b_T=1$: the unit runs backwards from $T$ to $S$

questions.question: A project network is directed and acyclic from start $S$ to finish $T$; each edge is an activity with a duration, and activities leaving a vertex wait for all activities entering it. The binary longest-path model sets $x_{ij}=1$ for the edges of a selected $S$-$T$ path. In an optimal solution, $x_{ij}=0$ for activity $(i,j)$. What does this mean?
options: The activity starts at time 0, before any other activity begins.
The activity is skipped, as it is not needed to finish the project.
The activity takes zero time, so it does not delay the project.
It is still carried out, just not on the selected longest chain.

questions.question: A project network has activities (edges with durations in weeks) $S\to1$: 4, $S\to2$: 3, $1\to2$: 2, $1\to3$: 5, $2\to3$: 4, $2\to T$: 6, $3\to T$: 3. An activity leaving a vertex may start only after all activities entering it finish, and there are no resource limits. What is the shortest possible project duration?
options: 9 weeks
13 weeks
12 weeks
27 weeks

questions.question: In a project network, activity $S\to1$ takes 2 days, $S\to2$ takes 7, $1\to2$ takes 3, $1\to T$ takes 6 and $2\to T$ takes 4; an activity leaving a vertex may start only when all activities entering it are finished. When can activity $2\to T$ start at the earliest?
options: At day 7
At day 12
At day 5
At day 10

questions.question: In the binary longest-path model of a project network, $x_{ij}=1$ selects edge $(i,j)$. At intermediate vertex 2 the entering edges are $S\to2$ and $1\to2$, and the leaving edges are $2\to3$ and $2\to T$. Which constraint belongs to vertex 2?

A project network has edges $S\to1$, $S\to2$, $1\to2$, $1\to T$ and $2\to T$. The binary model needs (outgoing $-$ incoming selected edges) $=1$ at $S$, $-1$ at $T$ and 0 at vertices 1 and 2. Which selection of edges satisfies all these balances?
options: $S\to1$ and $1\to2$
$S\to1$ and $1\to T$
$S\to2$, $1\to2$ and $2\to T$

questions.question: In a project network, activity $S\to1$ takes 5 weeks, $S\to2$ takes 2, $1\to T$ takes 4 and $2\to T$ takes 3, and activities leaving a vertex wait for all activities entering it. Activity $2\to T$ is shortened from 3 to 1 week. What is the shortest project duration afterwards?
options: 9 weeks
3 weeks
12 weeks
7 weeks

questions.question: The binary model maximizes $\sum d_{ij}x_{ij}$ over edges with balance $+1$ at $S$, $-1$ at $T$ and 0 at all other vertices. Why does the project longest path model require the network to be acyclic?
options: With a cycle, all durations on it become negative, so it is never worth selecting.
With a cycle, no selection can satisfy the balance constraints at the vertices of the cycle.
With a cycle, the model still gives the longest path, but the solver needs more steps.
With a cycle, the balances also allow a separate cycle to be selected, which adds length.

questions.question: A project network is directed and acyclic from start $S$ to finish $T$; each edge is an activity with a duration, and activities leaving a vertex wait for all activities entering it. Every duration is replaced by its negative and a shortest $S$-$T$ path is computed. Why does this give the longest path here, although shortest-path calculations usually take nonnegative lengths?
options: Negative lengths are always harmless, in any network with or without cycles.
No cycles exist, so no cycle of negative length can be traversed to lower the total.
Negating only reverses edge directions, so the same path is shortest and longest.
The negated path length equals the original one, as signs cancel along the path.

questions.question: A project network is directed and acyclic from start $S$ to finish $T$; each edge is an activity with a duration, and activities leaving a vertex wait for all activities entering it. There are no resource restrictions. A new precedence is added: some activity must now also wait for another one, modelled by an extra edge, and the network stays acyclic. How can the project duration change?
options: It can only stay equal or increase, since every old path still exists.
It can decrease, because the extra edge gives the work a better order.
It always stays the same, because no activity duration has changed.
It always increases, because every new edge creates a longer path.

questions.question: A project network has activities (edges with durations in weeks) $S\to1$: 4, $S\to2$: 3, $1\to2$: 2, $1\to3$: 5, $2\to3$: 4, $2\to T$: 6, $3\to T$: 3, and its duration is 13 weeks via $S$-1-2-3-$T$. Activity $2\to3$ is shortened from 4 to 1 week. What are the new duration and a longest path?
options: 9 weeks, via $S$-2-$T$
10 weeks, via $S$-1-2-3-$T$
12 weeks, via $S$-1-3-$T$
13 weeks, via $S$-1-2-3-$T$

questions.question: Activities in a project network: $S\to1$ takes 3 days, $S\to2$ 5, $1\to3$ 6, $2\to3$ 4, $1\to T$ 4 and $3\to T$ 2; an activity starts only when all activities entering its start vertex are done. If $1\to3$ is cut to 4 days, how long does the project take?
options: 9 days
7 days
10 days
11 days

questions.question: A project has activities $S\to1$ (3 days), $S\to2$ (5), $1\to3$ (6), $2\to3$ (4), $1\to T$ (4) and $3\to T$ (2), with duration 11. A new rule says activities leaving vertex 1 may also start only after $S\to2$ finishes, modelled by an extra edge $2\to1$ of duration 0. What is the new duration?
options: 16 days
13 days
9 days
11 days

questions.question: A project network is directed and acyclic from start $S$ to finish $T$; each edge is an activity with a duration, and activities leaving a vertex wait for all activities entering it. There are no resource restrictions, and some activity durations are reduced, none increased. How does 'at least one activity lying on some longest $S$-$T$ path is shortened' relate to 'the project duration decreases'?
options: It is required for a decrease, but does not guarantee one.
It guarantees a decrease, though a decrease can also happen without it.
It both guarantees a decrease and is required for one.
It neither guarantees a decrease nor is required for one.

questions.question: In an acyclic project network from $S$ to $T$ (edges are activities with durations; activities leaving a vertex wait for all entering ones), two facts give 'duration = longest path length': (i) the duration is at least the length of every $S$-$T$ path; (ii) starting each activity as early as precedence allows finishes at the longest path length. Which assumption does each fact need?
options: Both (i) and (ii) follow from precedence alone, whatever resources are available.
(i) follows from precedence; (ii) also needs activities to run in parallel freely.
(i) needs unlimited resources, while (ii) follows from the precedence rule alone.
Both rely only on acyclicity, which makes every path a sequence of activities.

questions.question: A network has edges $S\to1$ (length 2), $1\to T$ (3), $2\to3$ (4) and $3\to2$ (5). The binary model maximizes $\sum d_{ij}x_{ij}$ with $x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$ and balance (outgoing $-$ incoming selected edges) $=1$ at $S$, $-1$ at $T$, 0 at vertices 1, 2, 3. What is its optimal value?
options: 5, the length of the only $S$-$T$ path
9, the length of the cycle on 2 and 3
Unbounded, as the cycle can be repeated
14, the path plus the cycle on 2 and 3

questions.question: A project network has activities A: $S\to1$ (3 days), B: $S\to2$ (4), C: $1\to T$ (2) and D: $2\to T$ (1), so the longest path is 5 days. A and B both need the only crane and cannot run at the same time. What is now the shortest project duration?
options: 5 days
10 days
8 days
7 days
